title: Resilient Federated Learning on Embedded Devices with Constrained Network Connectivity
problem: Federated learning deployment on resource-constrained embedded devices faces communication bottlenecks when network connectivity is limited; bandwidth-heavy gradient transmission prevents practical federated training.
motivation: Federated learning preserves privacy but network overhead on embedded devices with constrained bandwidth limits participation and training efficiency.
method: When multiple resource-constrained devices train a shared model together (federated learning), they normally send all their updates back to a central server, but limited bandwidth makes this impractical. This method solves it by having each device check how different its local model is from the global shared model using a similarity score—and only transmit updates when that score indicates meaningful divergence, sending compressed updates instead. As training progresses and models converge toward the final solution, this transmission strategy automatically adapts to send less frequently.
key_novelty: The core idea is using a similarity score between the local and global models to adaptively decide when to transmit gradient updates, instead of using a fixed transmission policy.
contributions: Empirically validated on simulated and real embedded hardware
Maintains training convergence with reduced communication
limitations: Not discussed; specific convergence rates, final model accuracy, and overhead of similarity computation unclear.
primary_theme: Adaptive gradient compression for bandwidth-constrained federated learning
